amendments.because: On 2026-10-09 the owner explicitly chose the newer release for faster workflow after being told that it grants agents access outside the project without approval prompts. This accepts that host-access risk; it does not authorize bypassing tests, reviews, merge gates, or unrelated changes.

done_when: Forge runs v1.2.7 with its owner-approved full-access agent settings, existing merge and review gates, and financial-chat work preserved

findings.body: The hooks now source `.forge/hooks.sh` from the current checkout before invoking Forge. That tracked file is writable through the newly allowed Edit/Write tools, which are not covered by the Bash-only PreToolUse hook. An agent or branch can therefore replace it with arbitrary shell or a no-op `forge` function; the next hook then returns success without running the installed `forge hook deny`/approval checks, and SessionStart executes the branch-controlled shell with host access. `.codex/hooks.json` has the identical issue. The baseline called the installed Forge executable directly. This is new evidence not weighed by the prior proof-list review, and it conflicts with the ruling that full access does not authorize bypassing merge or review gates. The helper must be loaded from a trusted immutable location or verified before it is sourced.
